title: Landing Gear — Installation of Continuous Tyre Pressure Indicating at All Six Wheel Positions

issue.reason: Initial issue of the continuous tyre pressure indicating retrofit bulletin.

ata.title: Wheels and Brakes — Tyre Pressure Indicating

abstract: Retrofit of wheel-mounted tyre pressure sensors and gear leg receivers at all six positions, with the flight deck page and the maintenance report enabled by a brake control unit software load.

sections.planning_reason: The delivered aircraft has no tyre pressure indication and the maintenance programme requires a manual gauge check every four days, which short-sector operators do daily by choice because a deflated tyre found at the gate costs them a rotation. Two operators recorded eleven tyre changes in a year attributable to running a mate tyre under-pressure without knowing it, and one recorded a rejected take-off following a tread separation where the tyre had been under-inflated for at least six sectors.
sections.description: The bulletin installs a pressure sensor in each of the six wheels with a wheel-mounted transmitter and a receiver on the gear leg, replaces the brake control unit regulator with an item carrying the additional input, and loads the operational software that publishes the values.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on jacks and remove all six wheels. Install the axle manifold ESC959638-52 at each position using tension bolts AES343862-3E and washers AGS146031K9. Install the wheel sensor and transmitter in each wheel. Install the receiver on each gear leg and route the harness with the clamp kit D3240128079286. Replace the brake control unit regulator D3240120310957 with the item carrying the additional input and install the accumulator D3240121944667. Load the brake control unit operational software LH4C830E70C from the maintenance terminal. Install the wheels and torque to the value in the task. Do the inspection task AMM-C-32-40-13-200-025-A and confirm that all six positions report. Lower the aircraft, delete the four-day manual gauge check from the maintenance programme and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-11 and CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00137 to MSN C00680. Aircraft from MSN C00680 onward are already at the standard. Two aircraft with a non-standard wheel fit are excluded.
sections.material_note: Kit K3240-2008-01 contains six manifolds, six sensor and transmitter sets, two receivers, the harness, the regulator and the accumulator. Lead time is eighteen weeks. Removed regulators are returned to the supplier.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled A-check where the aircraft can be jacked, or within thirty-six months of the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

abstract: Retrofit of wheel-mounted tyre pressure sensors and gear leg receivers at all six positions, with the flight deck page and the maintenance report enabled by a brake control unit software load.

sections.planning_reason: The delivered aircraft has no tyre pressure indication and the maintenance programme requires a manual gauge check every four days, which short-sector operators do daily by choice because a deflated tyre found at the gate costs them a rotation. Two operators recorded eleven tyre changes in a year attributable to running a mate tyre under-pressure without knowing it, and one recorded a rejected take-off following a tread separation where the tyre had been under-inflated for at least six sectors. The first twenty embodiments produced a second finding of their own. The transmitter mass was judged insignificant at design and no wheel balance was called for; it is insignificant statically and it is not insignificant dynamically, and eleven of the twenty aircraft came back with a vibration complaint on the affected gear. The balance step is now required and the campaign was held until this revision was issued.
sections.description: The bulletin installs a pressure sensor in each of the six wheels with a wheel-mounted transmitter and a receiver on the gear leg, replaces the brake control unit regulator with an item carrying the additional input, and loads the operational software that publishes the values.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on jacks and remove all six wheels. Install the axle manifold ESC959638-52 at each position using tension bolts AES343862-3E and washers AGS146031K9. Install the wheel sensor and transmitter in each wheel and balance the wheel afterwards. Install the receiver on each gear leg and route the harness with the clamp kit D3240128079286. Replace the brake control unit regulator D3240120310957 with the item carrying the additional input and install the accumulator D3240121944667. Load the brake control unit operational software LH4C830E70C from the maintenance terminal. Install the wheels and torque to the value in the task. Do the inspection task AMM-C-32-40-13-200-025-A and confirm that all six positions report. Lower the aircraft, delete the four-day manual gauge check from the maintenance programme and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-11 and CIRRANE-13 aircraft from MSN C00137 to MSN C00680. Aircraft from MSN C00680 onward are already at the standard. Two aircraft with a non-standard wheel fit are excluded. Aircraft brought to the cold weather heat stack standard will need the effectivity of this bulletin reviewed, because the wheel instrumentation and the stack change compete for the same download path.
sections.material_note: Kit K3240-2008-01 contains six manifolds, six sensor and transmitter sets, two receivers, the harness, the regulator and the accumulator. Lead time is eighteen weeks. Removed regulators are returned to the supplier.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled A-check where the aircraft can be jacked, or within thirty-six months of the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Wheel balance step made mandatory after the transmitter is fitted following twenty embodiments with balance complaints; caveat added for aircraft planned for the cold weather heat stack standard
